anomalies.observed: SW7 pin 8 is listed as a node on both ESTOP_SINK1 and ESTOP_SINK2, tying the two independent e-stop sink nets together at the DIP-switch pin.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes separate ESTOP_SINK1 and ESTOP_SINK2 sink points for the two CAN/e-stop connectors, each gated independently. A single component pin cannot belong to two nets in a correct KiCad netlist; these nets should remain separate.

evidence.quote: an e-stop loop with multiple sink points (ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL) gated through single non-inverting buffers

anomalies.impact: The CAN Interface A and B e-stop sink inputs are shorted together, so cable-disconnect or switch state on one connector can affect the other and independent e-stop sinking is defeated.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; no supply rail, pull-up, driver, or other source is connected to it.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes should be connected to +3V3 or a switched 3.3V LED power net so the Ethernet/activity LEDs can conduct through their cathode resistors. The net name itself indicates a 3.3V LED power net, but the netlist shows it floating.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 cannot light because their anodes have no voltage source; Ethernet and Pi-activity LED indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: Both GND1 and GND2 pins of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are connected to the same GND net, and their VCC1/VCC2 supplies (SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V and 5V_switched_CAN) are also referenced to that same ground.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver requires separate primary-side and bus-side ground domains, and isolated supply domains, to provide the galvanic isolation implied by the specification's isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The intended galvanic isolation of the CAN interfaces is defeated; the CAN bus side is tied to the same ground as the controller side, so the board will not behave as an isolated CAN interface and may be susceptible to ground loops and noise.
